title: A standard smooth algebra over a field has dimension n-c at every point
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $B$ a $k$-algebra with a standard smooth presentation [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] given by integers $n\ge c\ge0$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $\alpha:k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak Q\subset B$ the dimension of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-dimension] is $n-c$: $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}B)=n-c$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T7 (label lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), part (7) and the last paragraph of its proof (a standard smooth algebra over a field is a local complete intersection with I/I^2 free of rank c, so it has dimension n − c, by Lemmas 00T5 lemma-smooth-over-field and 00SC lemma-lci); the remark after Definition 00S9 (definition-lci-field, lines 35827–35843: a global complete intersection k[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) of dimension n − c has dim(S_m) = n − c for all maximal ideals m and is equidimensional of dimension n − c); Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, line 27787: dim_x X = min dim S_m over maximal m containing the prime)

proof.text: (Reduction to the presentation ring.) Let $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)\subseteq P$ and $S=P/I$. Since $\alpha:S\to B$ is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras, the image of $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{1\le i,j\le c}$ in $S$ is $\alpha^{-1}$ of its image in $B$, a unit; so $S$ with the identity map is itself a standard smooth presentation over $k$ with the same $n\ge c\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. The map $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$, $\mathfrak Q\mapsto\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$, is a homeomorphism with inverse $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha^{-1}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; put $\mathfrak q=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$. By [def-kun-dimension] the dimension of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at $\mathfrak Q$ is the Krull dimension at $\mathfrak Q$ of its underlying topological space [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], and a homeomorphism carries open neighbourhoods of $\mathfrak Q$ to open neighbourhoods of $\mathfrak q$ and strict chains of irreducible closed subsets to strict chains of the same length. Hence $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}B)=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$, and it suffices to show $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-c$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), last paragraph (the statement is reduced to the standard smooth algebra k[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) itself)

proof.text: (Smoothness and the conormal module.) By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] the $k$-algebra $S$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-conormal-basis] the $S$-module $I/I^2$ is free with basis the classes of $f_1,\dots,f_c$, so $I/I^2\cong S^c$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), parts (1) and (3) and the first paragraph of its proof

proof.text: (Local complete intersection near $\mathfrak q$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection] applied to the smooth $k$-algebra $S$ of step 2, $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]: there are $g_i\in S$ ($i\in J$) with $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_iD(g_i)$ and every $S_{g_i}$ a global complete intersection over $k$. Choose $i$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(g_i)$ and put $g=g_i$; then $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and $S_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), last paragraph: 'We already know that k[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) is a local complete intersection by Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field)'; Definition 00S9 (definition-lci-field)

proof.text: (The conormal module at $\mathfrak q$ has rank $n-\dim_{\mathfrak q}$.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] to the presentation $S=P/I$, the prime $\mathfrak q$ and the element $g$ of step 3: $d:=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is an integer with $0\le d\le n$, and $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module of rank $n-d$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), last paragraph: 'since I/I^2 is free of rank c we see that k[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) has dimension n − c, by Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci)', implication (1) => (4) of 00SC with dim_q(S) = n − c' as in its statement

proof.text: (Comparing ranks; conclusion.) Localization at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ commutes with finite direct sums [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], so by step 2 $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}\cong(S^c)_{\mathfrak q}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^c$, while by step 4 $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^{n-d}$. The ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], in particular nonzero; tensoring $S_{\mathfrak q}^c\cong S_{\mathfrak q}^{n-d}$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ gives $\kappa(\mathfrak q)^c\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)^{n-d}$ as vector spaces, so $c=n-d$. Hence $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=d=n-c$, and by step 1 $\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}B)=n-c$.

split_report.summary: Proof written in 5 steps following Stacks 00T7, last paragraph of the proof (Route B of the brief: the lci route). Route A (through lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-dimension-differentials, Stacks 00TT (1)=>(3)) was rejected because the Stacks proof of 00TT (1)=>(3) itself uses this item (standard smooth over a field has dimension n−c), so it would create a cycle once 00TT is split. Steps: reduce from B to S=k[x]/(f) via the homeomorphism Spec alpha (identifying def-kun-dimension's dimension at a point with the topological one); S smooth and I/I^2 free on the f_j (00T7 (1),(3), two new Mathlib leaves); S lci over k (00T5, new unsplit node, with the new definition node for 00S9); (I/I^2)_q free of rank n − dim_q (00SC (1)=>(4) with 00P2, new unsplit node); compare ranks over the nonzero local ring S_q. Statement and stmt_deps kept.
